originality.rationale: Full primary-text inspection found the motivating two-class GD extension and an open maximal-extension problem in Demirov–Trifonov, but no global maximality criterion for this extension. Alon–Bourgain analyzes additive patterns in finite-field subgroups without the integer-set lifting lemma. The new equivalence handles arbitrary supersets and is not a direct stated corollary of either inspected primary work. Targeted comparisons found no stronger coverage; absolute priority remains uncertain.
residual_risks: The conversion from modular maximality to maximality among arbitrary integer GD supersets is elementary enough that an earlier unindexed or implicit derivation remains possible.
This is a criterion, not a classification of primes by congruence conditions, and not a construction of maximal extensions for all V_p.

value.rationale: The motivating recent paper asks for maximal GD supersets of residue-one progressions. The theorem decides, for every prime, whether its natural ±1 extension is globally maximal, including when a competitor is nonperiodic. The lifting principle is structural and provides exact finite tests and explicit infinite prime subfamilies in which maximality holds or fails. It does not overclaim solving all maximal-extension constructions.
